snippets.output: There are several anti-nausea medications, known as antiemetics, that can help patients keep fluids down and are particularly useful in managing nausea and vomiting.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates properties/definition of antiemetics as a category.

snippets.output: Ondansetron is a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist commonly used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery, and is available in oral, intravenous, and dissolvable tablet forms.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class, indications, formulations of ondansetron.

snippets.output: Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist that enhances gastrointestinal motility and is used to treat nausea and vomiting associated with gastroparesis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and postoperative conditions.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class, mechanism, indications of metoclopramide.

snippets.output: Prochlorperazine is a dopamine (D2) receptor antagonist effective in treating severe nausea and vomiting, including that caused by migraines and chemotherapy.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class and indications of prochlorperazine.

snippets.output: Promethazine is an antihistamine with antiemetic properties, often used to treat motion sickness, nausea, and vomiting.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class and indications of promethazine.

snippets.output: Dimenhydrinate is an antihistamine commonly used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class and indications of dimenhydrinate.

snippets.output: Scopolamine is an anticholinergic agent often used as a transdermal patch to prevent motion sickness and postoperative nausea and vomiting.
snippets.pattern_notes: Drug profile: class, formulation, and indications of scopolamine.
